questions.q: Why does this lesson say that simply telling Priya Nair 'security wins, the rollout waits' would have been the wrong move?
options: Because Mara Voss's technical concern wasn't actually valid
Because Lesson 23 established both positions as legitimate, and declaring one side the winner without addressing the other isn't a resolution, just a quieter version of the same conflict
Because Howard Okonjo had already overruled Mara in advance
Because Priya Nair outranks Mara Voss in Hartwell's org chart
questions.explain: A real resolution has to give both legitimate positions something real, not just declare a winner and call it settled.

questions.q: What actually ships during the planned maintenance outage window under Mara's compromise?
options: Nothing; the entire rollout is postponed until after the window
Identity consolidation and segmentation policy deploy in shadow mode — logging every access decision the policy would make, without yet blocking anything
Full enforcement ships immediately with no validation at all
Only a planning document is produced, with no technical work done
questions.explain: The window Operations needs is used for the actual identity and segmentation deployment — what's gated is enforcement, not the deployment itself.

questions.q: What are the validation gate's pass criteria, as stated in this lesson?
options: A simple vote among stakeholders on whether to proceed

Zero unplanned operational interruptions during the 14-day shadow-mode period, 100% of logged privileged access accounted for under the dual-check methodology, and any flagged discrepancy resolved before the gate closes
Whether Priya Nair personally approves of the result
A requirement that zero discrepancies of any kind ever occur anywhere at Hartwell
questions.explain: These are specific, measurable criteria — not a feeling or a vote — that determine whether full enforcement is safe to turn on.

questions.q: What happens if one of the validation gate's three criteria fails?
options: Enforcement ships anyway since the window is closing
Enforcement waits, and the specific failure identifies exactly what still needs fixing, rather than a vague 'not ready yet'
The entire zero-trust pilot program is cancelled
Priya Nair is given sole authority to decide whether to proceed
questions.explain: A specific failed criterion gives Mara an actionable next step, which is the whole point of a measurable gate over a vague go/no-go feeling.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between this compromise and the course's earlier material?
options: It is a completely new idea unrelated to anything covered earlier in the capstone
It reuses the same principle the capstone has returned to since Lesson 12 — don't trust a single check, and don't call something validated until independent evidence says so
It directly contradicts the lesson of the audit/SIEM discrepancy
It replaces the need for the dual-check methodology going forward
questions.explain: Shadow mode is simply another way of generating independent evidence before trusting a result, the same principle the dual-check automation already demonstrated.
